codeReview.summary: The commit only adds tests and does not implement the host/path canonicalization behavior required by the feature. The tests cover middleware helper responses for some host ownership cases, but they do not verify the protected guest-route sign-in redirect contract and the feature handoff itself records the live app-host guest-route flow still failing with ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS.

issues.description: This feature commit contains no production code changes, so the required canonicalization behavior is not actually implemented here. The feature description requires protecting guest routes, canonicalizing /guest, bouncing guest-owned app-host routes, and root-host /app/* handoff. This commit only broadens tests around existing behavior.

The test named 'bounces guest routes from the app host before preserving safe sign-in intent on root-host auth' stops after asserting a 200 response from handleRouting on the root-host guest URL. That does not verify VAL-FOUNDATION-004's required redirect to /auth/signin with a safe redirectedFrom value, so a key expected behavior remains uncovered by this feature's added tests.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The mission library already documents a local-dev limitation for multi-host guest-route validation, but the feature still had to discover and record that app.localhost guest-route browser checks loop in the local runtime. This environment quirk should remain clearly surfaced wherever feature reviewers/validators look first for route-host expectations.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: .factory/library/guest-routes.md notes multi-host live validation may require deterministic coverage, and mission AGENTS.md explicitly calls out VAL-FOUNDATION-013 as a known local-dev limitation; the host-and-route-canonicalization handoff still reports app.localhost/guest/bookings hitting ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS live.
